attributes.body_ja:
名詞（めいし）の「ため」（漢字（かんじ）では「為（ため）」）は、目的（もくてき）を表（あらわ）すときに使（つか）われます。「ため」は、それだけで使（つか）うことはできません。必（かなら）ず、目的（もくてき）を表（あらわ）すほかの言葉（ことば）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。「ため」のあとには、(A) が目的（もくてき）だとはっきりと示（しめ）すために、格助詞（かくじょし）の「に」が付（つ）くことも多（おお）いです。

この「ために」は、動詞（どうし）の辞書形（じしょけい）、または名詞（めいし）に「の」を付（つ）けた形（かたち）のあとに続（つづ）けて使（つか）われます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「ため」は、(A) が主（おも）な原因（げんいん）・理由（りゆう）となって (B) が起（お）こることを表（あらわ）すときにも使（つか）われます。

「ため」が過去（かこ）の出来事（できごと）に使（つか）われていたら、たいていこの原因（げんいん）・理由（りゆう）を表（あらわ）しています。
attributes.body:
ため (or 為（ため） in its kanji form) is a noun in Japanese that can be translated quite closely to 'sake' in English. However, it is classified as a non-independent word in Japanese, and must always be connected to another word which illustrates the 'sake' that ため is highlighting. The case marking particle に will often be added after ため, to show that (A) is a goal that something will be done to reach.

Due to this, ために can be translated as 'for the sake of (A)', or 'in order to (A)'.

To use ために, attach it to the end of verb in its non-past form, or a noun followed by の.

Fun Fact

Despite mainly being used to highlight goals, or things dictating an action, ため is also sometimes used to highlight events that have already taken place, and their results. Due to this, a more accurate translation of ため (in all of its uses) is 'in light of (A)'. This simply highlights that (A) is the primary or major event/thing that resulted in (B), or will result in (B).

When ため highlights past events, it is often translated simply as 'due to', or 'because of'.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: ために: Aims, Benefits, and Causation

attributes.body: Both can mean 'in order to' when expressing purpose and are often interchangeable in that usage, e.g. 健康維持のために運動する / 健康を維持するのに運動する ('I exercise in order to maintain my health.') However, ために can also express cause in certain contexts, which のに cannot, e.g. 雨のために試合が中止になった ('The game was canceled due to rain.')

first_relatable.title: ため(に)
first_relatable.meaning: For, For the sake of, In order to

attributes.body: These share the same core construction, using ため(に) to express 'in order to (A)' or 'due to (A)'. ため(に) is used within a sentence after a noun, verb, or adjective phrase. そのため is used at the beginning of a sentence to mean 'for that reason' or 'due to that', referring back to what was just said.

attributes.body: わけだ and ため(に) are similar in that both can be used when expressing a reason, but they mean quite different things. わけだ is used when drawing a conclusion, like the English 'so that's why (A)', while ため(に) on the other hand means 'for the sake of (A)' or 'due to (A)'.

attributes.body: Both can be translated as 'for (A)', but differ in nuance. 向き attaches directly to a noun and suggests suitability, e.g. 子ども向きの本 ('A book suitable for children') ため(に) connects to nouns with の and suggests intended benefit or purpose, e.g. 子どものための本 ('A book for children [designed to benefit them]')

second_relatable.title: ため(に)
second_relatable.meaning: For, For the sake of, In order to

attributes.body: んがため(に) can be considered an old-fashioned, literary form of ため(に). While both can express the idea of 'for the purpose of (A)' or 'in order to (A)', for example 生きんがために食べる 'eat (in order) to live' sounds like a much more formal and poetic version of 生きるために食べる (same meaning).

first_relatable.title: んがため(に)
first_relatable.meaning: In order to, To, For the purpose of

second_relatable.title: ため(に)
second_relatable.meaning: For, For the sake of, In order to

attributes.body: Both can express purpose, similar to 'in order to' or 'for that reason', e.g. 海外に行くためにパスポートを取った ('I got a passport in order to go abroad.') 海外に行くにはパスポートが必要だ ('A passport is necessary to go abroad.') Unlike ため(に), には also has broader uses, such as marking scope or perspective, e.g. 子どもには難しい ('It's difficult for children.')
